raw.description:
See your work in a new light.

At LUX Infusion, we’re reimagining infusion care to be more human, supportive, and connected. Inspired by lux—meaning light - we guide patients, providers, and partners through complex therapies with clarity, compassion, and confidence.

As a clinician-led, U.S.-based organization, we put people first - helping patients feel seen and supported through faster therapy starts, dedicated care coordination, and meaningful collaboration. Our commitment to inclusion, diversity, equity, and advancement (IDEA) is central to our culture, ensuring every team member feels valued and empowered to make a difference.

We’re looking for a Director, Talent Acquisition Strategy who wants their work to mean something—someone who brings care, accountability, and purpose to what they do every day.

Schedule & Location

Location: Overland Park, KS, or Plantation, FL or Remote

Schedule:

  • Monday - Friday, 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM

Why This Role Matters

As a Director, Talent Acquisition Strategy, you play a critical role in ensuring patients receive safe, effective, and timely specialty infusion therapies. Your expertise helps guide medication management, support clinical decision-making, and ensure every prescription is reviewed with accuracy and care.

In this role, you’ll contribute to work that:

  • Helps patients feel informed, supported, and confident throughout their treatment journey
  • Ensures safe and compliant specialty pharmacy operations
  • Supports clinicians, providers, and care teams through clinical expertise and collaboration
  • Advances positive patient outcomes through thoughtful medication management and oversight

Everything we do connects back to real people navigating complex healthcare journeys—and this role helps make that journey brighter.

What You'll Do

The Director, Talent Acquisition Strategy leads the development and execution of LUX Infusion's enterprise-wide talent acquisition strategy. This role is responsible for building a scalable, data-driven recruiting function that anticipates workforce needs and supports clinical, operational, professional, and leadership hiring across multiple states and markets.

The Director partners closely with executive leadership, Human Resources, Finance, Operations, and hiring leaders to translate business plans into workforce strategies; strengthen the employer brand and talent pipelines; optimize recruiting and onboarding processes; and use meaningful KPIs and analytics to improve hiring outcomes. The ideal candidate is a strategic, hands-on leader who can build systems, influence stakeholders, and operate effectively in a fast-paced, growing organization. Success in this role requires the ability to connect enterprise strategy with disciplined execution, create transparency through reliable data, and build a recruiting function that consistently delivers talent needed for growth.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

Talent Acquisition Strategy and Workforce Planning
• Develop and execute an enterprise-wide talent acquisition strategy aligned with LUX Infusion's growth plans, operating priorities, and long-term workforce needs.
• Partner with Finance, Operations, Human Resources, and business leaders to translate growth projections, turnover trends, labor availability, and productivity expectations into short- and long-term workforce plans.
• Create hiring forecasts, capacity models, prioritization frameworks, and recruiting resource plans that improve organizational readiness and reduce reactive hiring.
• Advise executive leadership on talent availability, geographic labor-market conditions, hiring risks, recruiting investments, and workforce implications of business decisions.
• Establish consistent, equitable, and legally compliant standards for job intake, candidate evaluation, interviewing, selection, and hiring decisions nationwide.
• Support workforce planning and talent acquisition needs for acquisitions, integrations, and new-market expansion as a recurring, core component of this role, not an incidental one.

Sourcing, Pipeline Development, and Employer Brand
• Build sustainable talent pipelines for critical, recurring, and difficult-to-fill positions across clinical, operational, professional, and leadership functions.
• Develop data-driven sourcing strategies using labor-market intelligence, geographic analysis, candidate and conversion data, referrals, professional networks, educational partnerships, and digital channels.
• Measure source quality and channel effectiveness to focus recruiting resources on approaches that produce qualified, durable hires drawn from broad candidate pools.
• Develop and maintain a compelling employer value proposition and partner with Marketing and Communications to strengthen the LUX Infusion employment brand.
• Create strategies for passive-candidate engagement, talent-community management, and market-specific outreach within a consistent national framework.

Recruiting Operations, Technology, and Onboarding
• Evaluate and optimize the end-to-end recruiting process, including requisition approval, sourcing, screening, interviewing, selection, offers, pre-employment requirements, and transition to onboarding.
• Establish recruiting service levels, standardized workflows, clear decision rights, and accountability for recruiters, hiring managers, and business partners.
• Lead the effective use and ongoing optimization of the applicant tracking system, including Greenhouse configuration, workflows, data integrity, reporting, user adoption, and compliance.
• Evaluate recruiting technology and automation opportunities that improve scheduling, candidate engagement, analytics, reporting, and team productivity, and confirm that any automated or AI-assisted screening tools comply with applicable law.
• Partner with Human Resources, IT, Compliance, and Operations to create a coordinated preboarding and onboarding experience, including licensure and credential verification and federal exclusion screening where applicable, that reduces delays and pre-start attrition and accelerates new-hire readiness.
• Use candidate and new-hire feedback to continuously improve the candidate, preboarding, and onboarding experience.

Analytics, KPIs, and Continuous Improvement
• Develop and maintain a comprehensive talent acquisition measurement framework, including KPIs, dashboards, targets, benchmarks, and reporting standards.
• Track and analyze measures such as hiring-plan attainment, time to fill, time to hire, cost per hire, source effectiveness, pipeline conversion, offer acceptance, candidate withdrawal, recruiter productivity, quality of hire, early retention, and stakeholder satisfaction.
• Conduct regular business reviews with leadership to assess performance, forecast needs, identify risks, and recommend corrective actions or resource changes.
• Ensure data integrity and disciplined system use so recruiting analytics are accurate, timely, consistent, and actionable.
• Develop leading and predictive indicators that allow the organization to anticipate hiring challenges rather than react after vacancies affect operations.

Leadership, Partnership, and Compensation Review

HR & Recruitment Coordinator

Start your career in HR and Talent Acquisition with BioPhorum

Are you a recent graduate looking to kick-start your career in HR? Are you naturally organised, curious, proactive and someone who enjoys working with people?

We're looking for an enthusiastic Graduate Resourcer & HR Assistant to join our People team at BioPhorum.

This is a great opportunity for someone at the start of their career who wants to gain hands-on experience across recruitment and HR, develop new skills and make a real contribution to a growing international business.

You don't need previous HR or recruitment experience. What matters most to us is your attitude, willingness to learn and desire to get stuck in.

About BioPhorum

BioPhorum is an international organisation that brings together leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to collaborate, share knowledge and solve some of the industry's biggest challenges.

Our people are at the heart of what we do, and our People team plays an important role in attracting, supporting and developing the talent that helps our business grow.

What will you be doing?

This is a varied role where you'll gain exposure to both recruitment and the wider HR function. You'll work closely with the Talent Partner and wider People team, learning how we attract great people, deliver a positive candidate experience and support employees throughout their time with BioPhorum.

Your responsibilities will include:

Recruitment and Talent Acquisition

  • Supporting the recruitment process from initial application through to interview and appointment.
  • Reviewing applications and identifying candidates who match our requirements.
  • Helping to source and engage potential candidates through different recruitment channels.
  • Coordinating interviews, communicating with candidates and keeping everyone updated throughout the process.
  • Supporting the preparation of interview materials and recruitment documentation.
  • Maintaining accurate candidate information and updating our recruitment systems.
  • Helping to ensure candidates have a positive experience when engaging with BioPhorum.

HR and People Support

  • Providing general administrative support across the employee lifecycle.
  • Supporting onboarding activities for new starters.
  • Maintaining accurate employee records and updating our HR system.
  • Preparing HR documentation and supporting day-to-day People team activities.
  • Helping with wider HR projects and initiatives, including employee engagement and internal communications.

You'll also have the opportunity to get involved in different projects, learn how the People team operates and build your understanding of the wider business.

What we're looking for

We're much more interested in your potential, attitude and approach than how much experience you already have.

You'll ideally be someone who:

  • Is a recent graduate, or has equivalent experience, and is keen to build a career in HR or recruitment.
  • Is proactive and takes initiative rather than waiting to be told what to do.
  • Is naturally organised, able to manage different priorities and has a good eye for detail.
  • Has strong communication skills and enjoys interacting with different people.
  • Is curious, asks questions and is keen to understand how things work.
  • Is confident using technology and comfortable learning new systems.
  • Takes responsibility for their work and follows things through.
  • Is positive, adaptable and happy to get involved wherever needed.

You don't need to tick every box. If you have the right attitude and are excited about developing a career in HR, we'd love to hear from you.

What will you get out of it?

This isn't just an entry-level administration role. It's an opportunity to build a strong foundation for a career in HR and Talent Acquisition.

You'll gain:

  • Hands-on experience across recruitment and the wider employee lifecycle.
  • Exposure to different areas of HR and how they support a growing international business.
  • The opportunity to work closely with experienced HR and Talent professionals.
  • Support, guidance and the chance to develop your skills and confidence.
  • Opportunities to contribute to projects and take ownership of your own responsibilities.
  • A role where you can make a genuine contribution and see the impact of your work.

Why BioPhorum?

At BioPhorum, we believe in bringing people together, sharing knowledge and making a difference. You'll be joining a collaborative team where people are encouraged to contribute ideas, take initiative and develop.

If you're looking for a role where you can learn, grow, challenge yourself and build a career in HR, this could be the perfect place to start.

Interested?

We'd love to hear from you. You don't need to have your career all figured out – just bring your enthusiasm, curiosity and willingness to learn.

We have a fantastic opportunity for a Learning and Development Business Partner, to join our Senior Leadership Team. This role will be remote with national travel.

Reporting directly to the Group Chief People Officer you will strengthen management capability and team effectiveness across EMED Group through practical, accessible learning. Working in partnership with operational leaders and People colleagues, deliver Management Acceleration Pathway (MAP) modules, bespoke local training and Insights-based development, while expanding and maintaining the online learning library.

This hands-on national role translates business and team development needs into learning that managers can apply every day, supporting consistent management practice, operational effectiveness and patient-centred service delivery.

Benefits for the role include

  • Competitive Salary
  • Annual car allowance
  • Performance related bonus
  • Private Healthcare
  • 33 days annual leave (inclusive of bank holidays) with the option to purchase additional leave through salary sacrifice.
  • Life Assurance
  • 24/7 online/telephone GP Consultation and access to prescriptions.
  • 2nd opinion medical support following diagnosis or where a colleague is on a treatment pathway.
  • Cash-plan benefits, providing colleagues the option of protecting themselves in case of illness and recuperation, including dental, optical, chiropody.
  • Access to mental health and physiotherapy consultations.
  • Access to legal advice on domestic issues e.g. motoring offences, wills and probate, and personal injury.
  • Long Service Recognition Scheme – recognising colleagues for their continued service after 5 years and at 5-year intervals with an increase in annual leave.

Role Responsibilities

  • Plan, coordinate and deliver MAP modules nationally through face-to-face workshops, virtual sessions and blended learning.
  • Build managers’ practical skills in communication, coaching, constructive feedback, delegation, team development, managing change and everyday management conversations.
  • Tailor examples, exercises and resources to operational settings while maintaining agreed MAP learning outcomes and delivery standards.
  • Work with HR team and subject matter experts to keep management content accurate, relevant and aligned with organisational policies and priorities.
  • Partner with operational leaders and HR Business Partners to understand local priorities and identify management and team development needs.
  • Design and deliver bespoke workshops, team development days and targeted training, adapting relevant MAP modules to meet local needs.
  • Support teams to strengthen communication, collaboration, clarity of responsibilities and shared ownership of agreed actions.
  • Promote MAP, team development and online learning through clear communications that explain the benefits and encourage participation.
  • Equip managers to deliver effective team briefings, listening conversations and communication during change through targeted training and practical resources.
  • Coordinate and deliver Insights-based development sessions in accordance with the chosen tool’s requirements and applicable practitioner accreditation.
  • Help managers and colleagues understand working preferences, adapt communication and collaborate effectively, without labelling people or making assumptions about capability.
  • Support teams to agree practical actions and revisit progress after sessions.
  • Maintain a prioritised development plan for new online modules, informed by management learning needs, recurring local requirements and organisational priorities.
  • Design and build engaging digital modules with clear learning objectives, practical scenarios, knowledge checks and supporting resources.
  • Use evaluation findings to improve programmes and inform priorities, distinguishing the contribution of learning from other factors affecting operational outcomes.

Do you have what it takes?

  • Experience designing and delivering management development and team learning in a multi-site or geographically dispersed organisation.
  • Strong facilitation skills, with the ability to engage different audiences through face-to-face and virtual delivery.
  • Ability to identify learning needs with stakeholders and translate them into practical, proportionate development solutions.
  • Experience creating digital learning modules using authoring tools and working with learning management systems.
  • Understanding of adult learning, blended learning and methods for evaluating learning application.
  • Clear written and verbal communication, strong stakeholder relationships and the confidence to influence without direct authority.
  • Ability to manage a national delivery schedule alongside bespoke requests and content development deadlines.
  • Commitment to accessible learning, confidentiality, respectful working relationships and patient-centred service delivery.
  • Ability to meet the national travel requirements of the role.

Desirable experience and qualifications

  • Relevant learning and development, training, coaching or organisational development qualification, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Accreditation in the Insights tool used by the organisation, or willingness to complete the required accreditation before independent delivery.
  • Experience supporting healthcare, patient transport, logistics or other operational, shift-based services.
  • Experience linking engagement feedback with team development and management learning.

About Us

EMED Group is an established healthcare logistics provider that enables access to health and social care through our four specialist divisions. We are one of the largest health and care partners to the NHS with 4,000 colleagues across over 60 bases UK-wide.

EMED Group is committed to pro-actively improving the wellbeing of our communities by providing access to vital health and social care services across the UK.

Job Overview

At Relativity, we build technology that helps people uncover the truth in complex data. Our software (SaaS) empowers legal professionals, governments, and organizations around the world to navigate high stakes matters with confidence, clarity, and integrity. By combining advanced AI, powerful analytics, and cloud-based technology, we help teams make sense of massive volumes of information and move critical work forward faster and more accurately. Every role at Relativity contributes to creating scalable, secure, and intelligent solutions with real-world impact—while fostering a culture where curiosity, collaboration, and inclusion thrive and where employees help shape the future of legal technology. 

Department Description:

The AI and Applied Sciences department at Relativity drives innovation by developing advanced AI solutions and applied research to solve complex legal and compliance challenges.

The Legal Data Intelligence SME will bring expertise as a practicing litigator and deep knowledge of discovery. You’ll draw on this expertise to help us build and evaluate our key generative AI capabilities. You’ll interface with other litigators, both helping us explain how our technology operates to them and taking their feedback and providing it back to our applied science team, conveying the nuances of both the technology and the needs of the litigator persona as you do so. This role bridges legal expertise with technical innovation, guiding the design and deployment of solutions that optimize data intelligence for legal workflows.

  • Work externally with our clients and our industry to explain how our generative AI systems work and to receive their feedback on the performance of our generative AI in analyzing and classifying documents, identifying information that needs to be protected, and extracting and curating knowledge.
  • Develop and deliver training and documentation for internal teams on legal data intelligence workflows and best practices.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • A Juris Doctorate and at least 3-5 years of experience as a practicing attorney; some but not all of this requirement may be satisfied by equivalent experience working for a legal service provider or legal technology vendor.
  • Deep interest in the use of generative AI to responsibly advance the practice of law and access to justice.
  • Strong and clear communicator, able to synthesize and communicate complex technical concepts and results to internal and external audiences.
  • Experience in discovery or legal technology platforms.
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams.

Preferred Qualifications :

  • Significant litigation experience and deep understanding of the processes of investigations and litigation, including discovery and pre-trial practice
  • At least 5 years of experience as a practicing attorney
  • Strong understanding of the traditional EDRM and broader Legal Data Intelligence use cases and workflows.

Business Intelligence (BI), Data Analysis, Data Governance, Data Intelligence, Data Visualization, Information Security, Legal Practices, Legal Research, Risk Management, Structured Query Language (SQL)

Location: Overland Park, KS, or Plantation, FL or Remote

Schedule:

  • Monday - Friday, 8:00 AM - 5:00 PM

Why This Role Matters

As a Director, Talent Acquisition Strategy, you play a critical role in ensuring patients receive safe, effective, and timely specialty infusion therapies. Your expertise helps guide medication management, support clinical decision-making, and ensure every prescription is reviewed with accuracy and care.

In this role, you’ll contribute to work that:

  • Helps patients feel informed, supported, and confident throughout their treatment journey
  • Ensures safe and compliant specialty pharmacy operations
  • Supports clinicians, providers, and care teams through clinical expertise and collaboration

This role is responsible for building a scalable, data-driven recruiting function that anticipates workforce needs and supports clinical, operational, professional, and leadership hiring across multiple states and markets.

The Director partners closely with executive leadership, Human Resources, Finance, Operations, and hiring leaders to translate business plans into workforce strategies; strengthen the employer brand and talent pipelines; optimize recruiting and onboarding processes; and use meaningful KPIs and analytics to improve hiring outcomes. The ideal candidate is a strategic, hands-on leader who can build systems, influence stakeholders, and operate effectively in a fast-paced, growing organization. Success in this role requires the ability to connect enterprise strategy with disciplined execution, create transparency through reliable data, and build a recruiting function that consistently delivers talent needed for growth.

• Develop and execute an enterprise-wide talent acquisition strategy aligned with LUX Infusion's growth plans, operating priorities, and long-term workforce needs.

• Create hiring forecasts, capacity models, prioritization frameworks, and recruiting resource plans that improve organizational readiness and reduce reactive hiring.
• Advise executive leadership on talent availability, geographic labor-market conditions, hiring risks, recruiting investments, and workforce implications of business decisions.
• Establish consistent, equitable, and legally compliant standards for job intake, candidate evaluation, interviewing, selection, and hiring decisions nationwide.
• Support workforce planning and talent acquisition needs for acquisitions, integrations, and new-market expansion as a recurring, core component of this role, not an incidental one.

HR & Recruitment Coordinator

Start your career in HR and Talent Acquisition with BioPhorum

Are you a recent graduate looking to kick-start your career in HR? Are you naturally organised, curious, proactive and someone who enjoys working with people?

We're looking for an enthusiastic Graduate Resourcer & HR Assistant to join our People team at BioPhorum.

This is a great opportunity for someone at the start of their career who wants to gain hands-on experience across recruitment and HR, develop new skills and make a real contribution to a growing international business.

You don't need previous HR or recruitment experience. What matters most to us is your attitude, willingness to learn and desire to get stuck in.

About BioPhorum

BioPhorum is an international organisation that brings together leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to collaborate, share knowledge and solve some of the industry's biggest challenges.

Our people are at the heart of what we do, and our People team plays an important role in attracting, supporting and developing the talent that helps our business grow.

What will you be doing?

This is a varied role where you'll gain exposure to both recruitment and the wider HR function. You'll work closely with the Talent Partner and wider People team, learning how we attract great people, deliver a positive candidate experience and support employees throughout their time with BioPhorum.

Your responsibilities will include:

Recruitment and Talent Acquisition

  • Supporting the recruitment process from initial application through to interview and appointment.
  • Reviewing applications and identifying candidates who match our requirements.
  • Helping to source and engage potential candidates through different recruitment channels.
  • Coordinating interviews, communicating with candidates and keeping everyone updated throughout the process.
  • Supporting the preparation of interview materials and recruitment documentation.
  • Maintaining accurate candidate information and updating our recruitment systems.
  • Helping to ensure candidates have a positive experience when engaging with BioPhorum.

HR and People Support

  • Providing general administrative support across the employee lifecycle.
  • Supporting onboarding activities for new starters.
  • Maintaining accurate employee records and updating our HR system.
  • Preparing HR documentation and supporting day-to-day People team activities.
  • Helping with wider HR projects and initiatives, including employee engagement and internal communications.

You'll also have the opportunity to get involved in different projects, learn how the People team operates and build your understanding of the wider business.

What we're looking for

We're much more interested in your potential, attitude and approach than how much experience you already have.

You'll ideally be someone who:

  • Is a recent graduate, or has equivalent experience, and is keen to build a career in HR or recruitment.
  • Is proactive and takes initiative rather than waiting to be told what to do.
  • Is naturally organised, able to manage different priorities and has a good eye for detail.
  • Has strong communication skills and enjoys interacting with different people.

You don't need to tick every box. If you have the right attitude and are excited about developing a career in HR, we'd love to hear from you.

What will you get out of it?

This isn't just an entry-level administration role. It's an opportunity to build a strong foundation for a career in HR and Talent Acquisition.

You'll gain:

  • Hands-on experience across recruitment and the wider employee lifecycle.
  • Exposure to different areas of HR and how they support a growing international business.

  • Support, guidance and the chance to develop your skills and confidence.
  • Opportunities to contribute to projects and take ownership of your own responsibilities.
  • A role where you can make a genuine contribution and see the impact of your work.

Why BioPhorum?

At BioPhorum, we believe in bringing people together, sharing knowledge and making a difference. You'll be joining a collaborative team where people are encouraged to contribute ideas, take initiative and develop.

If you're looking for a role where you can learn, grow, challenge yourself and build a career in HR, this could be the perfect place to start.

Interested?

We'd love to hear from you. You don't need to have your career all figured out – just bring your enthusiasm, curiosity and willingness to learn.

raw.title: Technical Program Manager - IP Backbone
raw.excerpt: About Nebius:Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy.
raw.description:
About Nebius:

Nebius is leading a new era in cloud infrastructure for the global AI economy. We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

Built by engineers, for engineers. From large-scale GPU orchestration to inference optimization, we own the hard problems across compute, storage, networking and applied AI.

Listed on Nasdaq (NBIS) and headquartered in Amsterdam, we have a global footprint with R&D hubs across Europe, the UK, North America and Israel. Our team of 1,500+ includes hundreds of engineers with deep expertise across hardware, software and AI R&D.

The IP Backbone TPM coordinates the planning and delivery of Nebius’s global IP backbone and Internet edge. The role connects data center launches, customer and platform demand, IP architecture, network engineering, procurement, and external providers so that sites have the routing, transit, peering, hardware, and address resources needed for service readiness and growth.

The TPM is accountable for end-to-end project coordination: defining scope with technical owners, building integrated plans, tracking dependencies and risks, driving decisions to closure, and confirming handover. Network Architecture and Engineering own technical standards and design decisions; engineers lead implementation. The TPM keeps those workstreams aligned and ensures the required outcomes are delivered.

Nebius Regions and HQ

In summer 2026, we introduced the concept of regions to remove dependence on the Amsterdam HQ and speed decision making. The regional change applies to procurement, logistics, and IT datacenter operations. Network infrastructure remains an HQ function because its architecture and design affect all sites.

Position Scope

Please note that Nebius is in a state of rapid growth. Due to this, the scope and responsibilities of the role will constantly evolve based on business and team needs.

Site and PoP Readiness

  • Coordinate IP connectivity due diligence for new data center and PoP locations.
  • Confirm the planned site role in the backbone and the required connectivity to regional and Super PoPs.
  • Track site dependencies such as rack space, power, security, cross-connects, cabling, hardware delivery, and carrier access.
  • Coordinate PoP build plans with IP Engineering, Layer 1 Planning, Data Center Operations, , Security, and Procurement.
  • Identify the boundary between IP and Layer 1 work early, including transport handoffs, demarcation points, and ownership of cross-connects.
  • Confirm that IP equipment and provider services are ready for installation, testing, and operational handover.

IP Connectivity Planning

  • Coordinate plans for IP transit, peering, private interconnects, and backbone connectivity in line with the global network strategy.
  • Track provider requirements, site availability, port capacity, cross-connects, delivery dates, commercial terms, and technical acceptance criteria.
  • Work with Procurement and network architects to gather and review ISP information using the provider qualification checklist. Use the completed assessment and architect input to support provider selection and record the decision and any conditions.
  • Plan connectivity for new data center launches, including the required paths from the front-end fabric to the Nebius backbone, transit providers, cloud on-ramps, and peering locations as applicable.
  • Maintain an integrated view of circuit, port, router, optics, and cross-connect dependencies so that a delivered service can be activated end to end.
  • Coordinate capacity growth and diverse connectivity plans before demand or a new launch creates a service constraint.

Internet Routing Resources and Security

  • Coordinate the lifecycle and accurate records for Nebius IPv4 and IPv6 address allocations, assignments, and utilization.
  • Maintain an operational view of ASN use and dependencies across regions, PoPs, transit providers, peers, and customer-facing services.
  • Coordinate the creation, review, and maintenance of AS-SETs, route objects, and ROAs with the responsible technical owners and relevant registries.
  • Track RPKI and IRR readiness as part of provider onboarding, routing changes, and new-site launches.
  • Coordinate remediation of resource or routing-security issues with Network Engineering and external providers.

Backbone Hardware and Supply

  • Maintain a forward-looking view of IP backbone hardware demand based on PoP builds, data center launches, capacity plans, and approved architecture.
  • Coordinate hardware planning and delivery for routers, line cards, optics, spares, software entitlements, and related components.
    • Standard platforms are Juniper MX304 routers for peering borders, Juniper PTX10002 routers for data center borders, and Cisco 8000 Series routers for Cloud Interconnect (CIC) and cloud on-ramps.
  • Work with IP Engineering to translate approved designs into complete, validated bills of materials and deployment requirements.
  • Track forecasts, purchase requests, supplier commitments, lead times, delivery allocations, and regional logistics with Network Supply and Procurement.
  • Coordinate supply for PoP out-of-band equipment (currently MikroTik, with future SD-WAN platforms under consideration), console access, and PoP management networks. Security appliances are outside this role’s hardware scope.
  • Identify supply risks early and coordinate mitigation options with technical owners, procurement, and project stakeholders.
  • Keep project schedules aligned with hardware readiness, site readiness, and service activation milestones.

Delivery and Launch Coordination

  • Build and maintain integrated delivery plans for IP backbone projects, PoP builds, provider services, and data center launches.
  • Coordinate work across IP Architecture, IP Engineering, Layer 1 Planning, Data Center Operations, Construction, Security, Procurement, and providers.
  • Define milestones, prerequisites, owners, acceptance criteria, and handover requirements for each workstream.
  • Drive resolution of blockers and escalate risks that could affect site launch, customer commitments, capacity, or network resilience.
  • Coordinate testing, service activation, routing turn-up, documentation, and operational handover with the engineering and operations teams.
  • Maintain clear status reporting for project scope, schedule, dependencies, decisions, risks, and actions.

Operations and Capacity Management

  • Track IP backbone and Internet edge capacity against forecast demand, data center growth, customer requirements, and platform launches.
  • Coordinate port, router, transit, peering, address-resource, and hardware expansion before capacity constraints affect service readiness.
  • Maintain accurate records of PoPs, providers, circuits, ports, ASNs, address allocations, AS-SETs, ROAs, and deployment status in the agreed systems of record.
  • Support incident follow-up and provider escalations when delivery or service issues affect backbone availability.
  • Review completed projects with technical and operations teams, capture lessons learned, and improve planning and handover processes.
  • Support ongoing improvements to resiliency, routing security, provider diversity, and operational readiness.

Working Boundaries with Layer 1 Planning

IP and Layer 1 TPMs share delivery responsibility for PoP and data center connectivity projects. The IP TPM coordinates the IP service outcome: routing, transit, peering, IP address resources, IP hardware, and service activation. The Layer 1 TPM coordinates the physical and optical transport outcome: fiber routes, wavelengths or dark fiber, DWDM systems, ILAs, and the transport path to the agreed handoff.

For shared projects, the two TPMs should maintain one integrated milestone plan, agree the service demarcation and handoff points with engineering, and assign a clear owner to each dependency. Technical design and configuration decisions remain with the relevant architecture and engineering owners.

Internal Operating Context

Nebius infrastructure supports Nebius Cloud Platform, Nebius Token Factory, Meta, Microsoft, and selected bare-metal customers. The IP backbone TPM works with product and infrastructure stakeholders to translate Nebius Cloud launches and requirements into deliverable connectivity plans. This scope covers Nebius Cloud by default; Internet access for a bare-metal customer is included when that customer specifically requests it. Cloud Interconnect requirements may require dedicated on-ramp planning.

For provider onboarding, Procurement coordinates the commercial process and issues the qualification questionnaire. The TPM coordinates technical due diligence with Backbone Architecture and Engineering, tracks completion, and records the approval decision and follow-up actions. The TPM coordinates the provider assessment and selection process with Procurement and the network architects, using the qualification checklist and architect input to reach and document the decision.

Security Project Coordination

The TPM may coordinate IP security and DDoS-related projects that affect the backbone or Internet edge. Security Architects lead these projects and own the security architecture and technical decisions. The TPM coordinates scope, dependencies, milestones, risks, stakeholder communication, and delivery handover with Security, Network Architecture, Engineering, Procurement, and providers as needed.

Key Collaborators

Function

Typical contribution

IP / Backbone Architecture

Defines architecture and technical standards; provides technical input to provider selection and design decisions

IP Engineering

Owns detailed design, configuration, implementation, testing, and technical handover

Front End Fabric Deploy Team

Ensures that OOB connectivity is ready, and that CAB + Border related deploy work is completed and unblocks this team.

Layer 1 Planning / DWDM Engineering

Delivers transport connectivity and coordinates shared PoP or site dependencies

Network Supply and Procurement

Forecasts and sources hardware and services; coordinates provider qualification and commercial processes

Data Center Operations and Construction

Delivers site access, space, power, cabling, cross-connect, and readiness dependencies

Product and customer teams

Provides launch dates, demand forecasts, and customer or platform requirements

Security Architects

Lead IP security and DDoS projects and own security architecture decisions

ISPs, peers, exchanges, and cloud providers

Deliver transit, peering, interconnection, and related services

About Nebius

Nebius AI is an AI cloud platform with one of the largest GPU capacities in Europe. Launched in November 2023, the Nebius AI platform provides high-end, training-optimized infrastructure for AI practitioners. As an NVIDIA preferred cloud service provider, Nebius AI offers a variety of NVIDIA GPUs for training and inference, as well as a set of tools for efficient multi-node training.

Nebius AI owns a data center in Finland, built from the ground up by the company’s R&D team and showcasing our commitment to sustainability. The data center is home to ISEG, the most powerful commercially available supercomputer in Europe and the 16th most powerful globally (Top 500 list, November 2023).

Nebius’s headquarters are in Amsterdam, Netherlands, with teams working out of R&D hubs across Europe and the Middle East.

Nebius AI is built with the talent of more than 500 highly skilled engineers with a proven track record in developing sophisticated cloud and ML solutions and designing cutting-edge hardware. This allows all the layers of the Nebius AI cloud – from hardware to UI – to be built in-house, distictly differentiating Nebius AI from the majority of specialized clouds: Nebius customers get a true hyperscaler-cloud experience tailored for AI practitioners. We’re growing and expanding our products every day.

If you’re up to the challenge and are excited about AI and ML as much as we are, join us!

Pay Transparency

We offer competitive compensation and benefits packages. Actual compensation will be determined based on job-related factors, including experience, skills, qualifications, the level at which the candidate is hired, and geographic location, consistent with applicable law.

Base Compensation Range
$180,000—$230,000 USD

Benefits & Perks:

  • Competitive compensation
  • Career growth and learning opportunities
  • Flexibility and ownership
  • Collaborative and innovative culture
  • Opportunity to work on impactful AI projects
  • International environment and talented teams

What's it like to work at Nebius:

Fast moving - Bold thinking - Constant growth - Meaningful impact - Trust and real ownership - Opportunity to shape the future of AI

Equal Opportunity Statement:

Nebius is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace and to providing equal employment opportunities in all aspects of employment. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the country in which they apply and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility as a condition of hire.

If you need accommodations during the application process, please let us know.

raw.excerpt: Wing Assistant is a venture-backed, Silicon Valley-based startup with global operations.
raw.description:
Wing Assistant is a venture-backed, Silicon Valley-based startup with global operations. We match US businesses with dedicated, fully managed remote professionals (executive assistants, customer service reps, healthcare admins, bookkeepers, and more) and run the delivery behind them: recruiting, onboarding, management, and support. We're also building exciting AI technologies to help clients get even more done across our Wing suite and sister companies we operate in the AI space.

Our talent and delivery teams are based in the Philippines; our clients are mostly in the US; our leadership works across Hong Kong and the US. We've scaled fast. Now we're obsessed with getting every customer we win live quickly, and keeping them for the long haul.

The Role

    The biggest lever on Wing's growth is what happens after a customer signs: how quickly they get value, and how long they stay. We're hiring one person to own the entire post-sale journey (onboarding, activation, and retention) from the moment a deal closes to month 12 and beyond.

    This is not an advisory role. You won't hand off a deck and walk away. You'll diagnose where and why customers stall or leave, build the systems and tools to fix it, and hold multiple teams accountable to the numbers. If you've spent years recommending changes and want to be the person who actually makes them happen, this is that job.

What you'll own

  • The onboarding pipeline. Every new account from signed deal to fully live. You know where every account sits, where it's stuck and why, and you make sure it moves faster.
  • Activation and early-life health. The first months decide whether a client stays. Define what a healthy start looks like, spot accounts going off track and intervene early.
  • Retention and churn as numbers. Define them, measure them and break them down (logo vs. revenue, early-life vs. mature, by role, segment, acquisition channel and team). Set the targets and own the trend lines.
  • Root-cause analysis. Funnels, cohorts, survival curves, leading indicators. Go beyond the dashboard into the qualitative and raw data to find what really drives outcomes.
  • Process improvement. Map the handoffs across teams, find the friction, redesign the process, run experiments and measure the impact.
  • Building tools. Vibe-code dashboards, alerts and workflow tools using Claude and other AI coding tools. Ship useful things in days, not quarters.
  • Deep data work. Write the SQL, reconcile the sources and build the models. When two systems disagree, you find out which one is right and why.
  • Stakeholder leadership. Work with sales, recruiting, customer success, finance, product and our Philippines operations team: people from very different backgrounds, functions and time zones. Drive change through clarity and evidence often without direct authority.
  • Reporting to leadership. A crisp weekly view of pipeline, activation and retention health: what changed, and what you're doing about it.

What success looks like

    First 30 days: You've mapped the customer journey end to end, have access to every relevant data source, and have built trusted baselines for the metrics you own.

    First 60 days: You've identified the highest-impact opportunities with hard evidence, launched the first interventions, and shipped your first tools.

    First 90 days: You can show measurable improvement on at least one core metric, yourun a weekly operating cadence, and the tools you built are used daily by the teams.

Working Arrangements

  • Remote, full-time role. Occasional in-person meetings in Hong Kong.
  • Location: Hong Kong.
  • Hours: Our clients and many team members operate on US time. Your working day will generally run from the evening into the night, Hong Kong time. This is a core requirement of the role, not an occasional ask.
  • Travel: Occasional trips to our operation center in the Philippines.
  • Pace: This is an intense, high-ownership role in a fast-moving company. Expect high standards, tight feedback loops and real accountability for results. It's a great fit if you want to grow fast and see your work move the numbers, and probably not the
    right fit if you're looking for a steady 9-to-5.
  • Commitment: This is a high-ownership, full-time role, and we expect it to be your only professional commitment. If you have other employment, consulting work or business interests, please mention them when you apply so we can discuss them openly.

How to apply

  • Send your CV and a short note (no more than 200 words) about a time you found the number nobody else had noticed, and what happened next. Links to anything you've built with AI tools are a strong plus.

  • Shortlisted candidates will complete a practical case exercise using real-world style data.

Fine Print

  • Background and reference checks. Final-stage candidates may be asked to complete background and reference checks, with their consent and in line with applicable law.
  • Equal opportunity. Wing is an equal opportunity employer. We hire on merit and welcome applicants of every background, regardless of race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, marital or family status, nationality or any other characteristic protected by law.

raw.description:
Bloom is a full-service workplace design consultancy, proudly supporting Poppy & Peonies in their search for a Director of Brand & Social to join their dynamic team. As Talent Advisors, we serve as the bridge between our Bloom Partner and you throughout the recruitment process. At Bloom, we don’t rely on automated tools to sift through applications—every resume is carefully reviewed by a real person to ensure a fair and consistent interview process. If selected, you’ll join Poppy & Peonies directly as a valued member of their team. We’re excited to consider your application! Please note that applications will be accepted throughout the holiday season. Thank you for your patience and interest in this opportunity!

Hi, I’m Natalie Dusome, Founder and CEO of Poppy & Peonies, a fun and energetic brand that believes styles and function should co-exist. We’re passionate about creating practical pieces that help make life a little easier and lighten the load, literally.

Building Poppy & Peonies has been a wild adventure. The journey began when my daughter Poppy was born and my accessories no longer worked with my new life as a mom, I needed bags with pockets and organization that looked cool and had functionality. I couldn’t find it, so I decided to create it, and in 2015 Poppy & Peonies was born.

We’ve come a long way in five years – from filling orders in my basement to appearing on Dragons’ Den, and now, expanding into new product categories and collaborating with some exciting influencers and brands. I’d be lying if I said it’s been nothing but smooth sailing, but thanks to our incredible community, we’ve never felt more loved and supported!

We believe in our responsibility to care for our environment and we are passionate about preserving the health and welfare of our planet, and the animals that live on it. All of our bags are made from high-quality vegan leather, and our entire product line is vegan, cruelty-free, and PETA-approved. We ship our products plastic-free and we use a combination of recycled, compostable, and biodegradable materials to mitigate shipping waste, and we are constantly looking for new ways to make our products and supply chain more sustainable to reduce our carbon footprint.

About the Role

The Director of Planning will lead the integrated Demand Planning, Supply Planning, and Inventory Planning functions at Poppy & Peonies.

This role is responsible for translating commercial plans into actionable inventory and purchasing strategies, ensuring the right products are available in the right quantities, at the right locations, and at the right time.

Working closely with Merchandising, Product Development, Marketing, Finance, Sourcing, and Operations, the Director will establish a disciplined Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) process that balances revenue growth, product availability, inventory productivity, and cash flow.

The ideal candidate combines strong analytical and financial acumen with hands-on planning experience in a fast-paced consumer products environment. They are comfortable working at both strategic and operational levels, building scalable processes while actively managing forecasts, inventory, and purchasing decisions.

The Opportunity

    Demand Planning & Forecasting

  • Own the end-to-end demand forecasting process across all product categories, sales channels, and markets.

  • Develop and maintain rolling demand forecasts at the SKU, category, channel, and distribution center levels.

  • Partner with Merchandising, Marketing, and eCommerce to incorporate product launches, promotional activities, seasonality, marketing investments, and business growth assumptions into forecasts.

  • Lead forecast reviews, analyze actual performance against projections, identify demand trends, and continuously improve forecast accuracy.

  • Develop forecasting methodologies for new product introductions, core replenishment products, and seasonal collections.

  • Identify demand risks and opportunities early and recommend actions to optimize sales and inventory performance.

    • Supply Planning & Purchasing

raw.description:
Terms of Reference (ToR): Rapid Assessment of the Context of and Opportunities for Refugees and Displaced Youth in Nigeria.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Interested applicants are encouraged to submit their applications early.

  1. Background

Nigeria hosts substantial populations of Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs), refugees and asylum seekers, with displacement driven by armed conflict, insecurity, intercommunal tensions and climate-related pressures. As of 1 October 2026, available figures indicate approximately 3.7 million IDPs and 141,688 refugees and asylum seekers.

Displaced youth aged 18–35 face multiple barriers to education, skills development, employment, entrepreneurship and economic participation. These include disrupted educational pathways, limited access to training and financial services, documentation requirements, restricted economic opportunities, and social exclusion. Young women and youth with disabilities may experience additional barriers. These barriers may be compounded by intersecting factors such as age, gender, disability, displacement status, socioeconomic circumstances and geographic location. Gender norms, unpaid care responsibilities, safety concerns and limited accessibility may further constrain participation in education and economic opportunities. However, the circumstances of refugees, asylum seekers and IDPs differ considerably, including in terms of their legal status, access to services, institutional support and opportunities for economic inclusion.

These differences are also shaped by geography, local economic conditions, government policies and the capacities and incentives of institutions responsible for supporting displaced populations.

The Mastercard Foundation, through its partnership with WUSC under the DREEM project, seeks to strengthen opportunities for refugees and displaced youth (RDPs) to access education, develop relevant skills and participate meaningfully in economic life. In Nigeria, there is particular interest in understanding opportunities to strengthen the inclusion of internally displaced youth, alongside refugees and asylum seekers.

A rapid contextual assessment is therefore proposed to consolidate existing evidence, examine the institutional and structural factors shaping RDP inclusion, and identify practical opportunities for future programming, partnerships and policy engagement.

2. Purpose of the Assessment

The assessment aims to generate practical, context-specific evidence on the barriers and
opportunities affecting the inclusion of refugees and internally displaced youth in Nigeria,

particularly in education, skills development, employment, entrepreneurship and broader economic participation.It will examine the policy, institutional, socioeconomic and political economy factors shaping these opportunities, including the roles and incentives of relevant government institutions, private sector actors, development partners and refugee- and IDP-led organizations. The assessment will apply an intersectional lens to understand how barriers and opportunities differ among displaced youth, particularly young women, youth with disabilities and those experiencing multiple forms of exclusion.

The assessment will inform the Mastercard Foundation's and DREEM's understanding of th Nigerian context and help identify feasible areas for programmatic support, institutional

partnerships and policy engagement.

raw.description:
At Clover, the Business Enablement team leads our technological advancement while ensuring robust security and compliance. We deliver user-friendly corporate applications, manage complex data ecosystems, and provide efficient tech solutions across the organization. Our goal is simple: we make it easy for the business to do what’s right for Clover.

We’re hiring a Director of Product to build and lead a product function in Clover's new R&D function. Reporting directly to the CTO, the scope of you and your team will span health-plan, care services, and corporate technology.

This is a player-coach role. You will personally work through difficult product questions while developing a small, flat team of product managers and embedded product operations staff. Most PM assignments will pursue one or two defined outcomes through repeated research and experiments. A small number of senior assignments will require judgment across ambiguous problem spaces to identify and shape the next project worth doing.

You will lead product craft across R&D from the outset, while drawing on the product expertise of Counterpart, our separate technology subsidiary. The surface area is large, and Product missions and capacity will evolve with the business needs and evidence.

You’ll work with empowered teams and individuals: our engineers work directly with users, exercise product judgment, and own technical execution. Many operational needs are clear and practical technical solutions are available; the harder work is resolving details, ownership, and adoption. Our bias is to build the simplest useful system and iterate quickly. You will recognize when engineers and operating owners can advance directly, where a PM can improve a defined outcome, and where substantial product or design discovery is needed.

As a Director of Product, you will:

  • Build and develop the product team. Hire for the work, give direct feedback, coach research and measurement, and grow people’s judgment while keeping the structure proportionate to the team.
  • Build a culture within product and engineering that values incremental progress toward measurable outcomes, clear stakeholder communication, and aggressive AI-forward productivity.
  • Understand the member journey across plan and clinical operations. Observe the work, review interactions and data, and connect apparent technology problems to the underlying needs of members and staff.
  • Choose focused product missions with business and engineering partners. Decide where dedicated product attention will help and match the assignment to the uncertainty: a defined improvement mission or senior discovery across a broader problem space. Establish useful baselines, define success, test assumptions, and change course when the evidence warrants it.
  • Personally investigate ambiguous opportunities. Turn them into a clear problem, evidence of value, a plausible approach, and a useful first delivery or learning milestone.
  • Develop an embedded Product Operations function that connects frontline observation, testing, training, and adoption to product and engineering decisions.
  • Partner closely with product leaders in other organizations, Special Project Leads, clinical leaders, and operating owners. Make ownership clear across shared journeys and capabilities.
  • Use AI directly to investigate ideas, build and test prototypes, and run bounded experiments. Check the outputs and use what you learn to choose the next step. Work with engineering and operating owners to take promising experiments into production; engineering retains technical delivery and readiness, and operating owners accept the resulting workflow.

Success in this role looks like:

  • First 90 days: You understand the initial member and operational journeys, have selected focused product missions with engineering and operating partners, and can explain where teams can advance directly. You are personally advancing a difficult product question, coaching the initial PM work, and establishing credible evidence from an improvement or experiment.
  • First six months: PMs exercise stronger judgment and independently advance their assigned missions. Senior discovery produces focused projects and well-supported decisions to defer or stop. Shipped changes are being used, and product decisions connect to measurable improvements in member experience, operational effectiveness, or unit economics.

You should get in touch if:

  • You have led and developed product managers while remaining personally involved in discovery, prioritization, and difficult product decisions.
  • You have built or substantially shaped a product function and are comfortable starting with a small team and an evolving remit.
  • You have improved products used in real operational workflows and can connect software, human work, business economics, and adoption.
  • You use AI heavily in your own work and have a practical view of its capabilities and limitations, and strong hypotheses about its future.
  • You are technically fluent in systems, APIs, data, and AI behavior. You can independently investigate an idea, build and test a prototype, and run a bounded experiment using AI. You can understand the architectural implications of the products you help design.
  • You use research, data, and experiments to make decisions, and can distinguish a promising observation from evidence strong enough to act on.
  • You work effectively with engineers who exercise broad judgment and with operating leaders who own their businesses. You build trust through direct relationships and clear decisions.

Benefits Overview:

  • Financial Well-Being: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.
  • Physical Well-Being: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.
  • Mental Well-Being: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.
  • Professional Development: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.

Additional Perks:

  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities
  • Reimbursement for office setup expenses
  • Monthly cell phone & internet stipend
  • Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams
  • Paid parental leave for all new parents
  • And much more!

About Clover: We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.

We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.

From Clover’s inception, Diversity & Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records. We are an E-Verify company.

Final pay is based on several factors including but not limited to internal equity, market data, and the applicant’s education, work experience, certifications, etc.

A reasonable estimate of the base salary range for this role is:
$207,000—$270,000 USD

Job Overview

You will be responsible for planning, creating, executing, and optimizing B2B email marketing campaigns using Klaviyo.

The role combines email strategy, copywriting, campaign execution, audience segmentation, automation, testing, and performance analysis. You should understand how to communicate technology and business value clearly without making emails feel overly promotional or generic.

You will work closely with the marketing, content, SEO, sales, and product teams to develop email campaigns aligned with Uvation's business objectives.

Key Responsibilities

  • Plan and execute B2B email marketing campaigns from concept through deployment and reporting.
  • Build and manage email campaigns and automated flows in Klaviyo.
  • Develop email campaigns for prospects, leads, customers, partners, and other relevant audiences.
  • Write clear, engaging, and conversion-focused email copy.
  • Develop lead-nurturing and email sequences based on audience stage, behavior, and intent.
  • Segment email audiences based on factors such as industry, engagement, interests, funnel stage, and customer profile.
  • Create campaigns around Uvation's AI infrastructure, AI data centers, AI factories, GPU computing, cloud, enterprise technology, and services.
  • Develop newsletters, product updates, educational campaigns, promotional campaigns, and thought-leadership emails.
  • Work with the content team to repurpose long-form content, whitepapers, research, case studies, and other assets into email campaigns.
  • Collaborate with sales teams on lead-nurturing and sales-support campaigns.
  • Develop compelling subject lines, preview text, CTAs, and email messaging.
  • Conduct A/B tests on subject lines, copy, CTAs, content structure, timing, and other campaign elements.
  • Monitor campaign performance, including open rates, click-through rates, conversions, unsubscribe rates, engagement, and other relevant metrics.
  • Analyze campaign results and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Maintain email lists, segmentation, campaign workflows, and data hygiene.
  • Develop and optimize automated email journeys and lifecycle campaigns in Klaviyo.
  • Check email rendering across major email clients and devices.
  • Make basic HTML/CSS adjustments to email templates when required.
  • Work with the marketing team to maintain consistent brand voice and messaging.

What We're Looking For

  • Experience in B2B email marketing.
  • Hands-on experience with Klaviyo.
  • Excellent written English and strong email copywriting skills.
  • Ability to write concise, engaging, and persuasive email copy.
  • Understanding of B2B buying journeys and lead nurturing.
  • Experience with audience segmentation and targeted email campaigns.
  • Experience creating and managing automated email flows.
  • Strong understanding of email marketing metrics and campaign performance.
  • Ability to analyze campaign results and make data-driven improvements.
  • Basic knowledge of HTML and CSS, with the ability to understand and make simple changes to email templates.
  • Understanding of email formatting and responsive email design.
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly around links, formatting, personalization, and rendering.
  • Ability to understand technical products and communicate their value to business and technology audiences.
  • Comfortable working independently in a remote environment.
  • Strong collaboration skills with marketing, sales, content, and product teams.
  • Native English-speaking candidates preferred/required.

Klaviyo Skills

The candidate should be comfortable working with Klaviyo for:

  • Campaign creation and scheduling
  • Automated flows
  • Audience segmentation
  • Lists and profiles
  • Personalization
  • Conditional logic
  • A/B testing
  • Email templates
  • Campaign reporting
  • Flow performance analysis
  • Engagement-based targeting
  • List hygiene
  • Basic deliverability practices

HTML & Email Development

Basic HTML/CSS knowledge is required. The candidate should be able to:

  • Understand the basic structure of an HTML email.
  • Make simple edits to existing email templates.
  • Modify text, links, buttons, images, spacing, and basic formatting.
  • Identify and fix simple HTML formatting issues.
  • Understand responsive email considerations.
  • Review emails across different devices and email clients.
  • Work with existing branded email templates without requiring a developer for routine changes.

This is not a front-end developer role. Strong email marketing skills are more important than advanced coding ability.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in B2B technology, SaaS, IT, infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud, or another technical industry.
  • Experience marketing to enterprise technology audiences.
  • Experience creating sophisticated automated email sequences and nurture journeys.
  • Familiarity with CRM and marketing automation systems.
  • Basic understanding of SEO and content marketing.
  • Experience working with sales teams on lead generation and lead nurturing.
  • Experience using analytics to optimize email campaigns.
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted marketing and content tools.

WHO WE ARE

Zeta Global (NYSE: ZETA) is the AI-Powered Marketing Cloud that leverages advanced artificial intelligence (AI) and trillions of consumer signals to make it easier for marketers to acquire, grow, and retain customers more efficiently. Through the Zeta Marketing Platform (ZMP), our vision is to make sophisticated marketing simple by unifying identity, intelligence, and omnichannel activation into a single platform – powered by one of the industry’s largest proprietary databases and AI. Our enterprise customers across multiple verticals are empowered to personalize experiences with consumers at an individual level across every channel, delivering better results for marketing programs. Zeta was founded in 2007 by David A. Steinberg and John Sculley and is headquartered in New York City with offices around the world. To learn more, go to .

Role Overview

This is a hands-on Principal Infrastructure Security opportunity within the DevSecOps practice that strengthens security across our primarily AWS-based infrastructure and software delivery. Partner with AppSec and InfoSec to prevent issues and respond effectively when they arise. This is a player-coach role: set strategy while staying close to the technical work.

What You'll Do

  • Define and execute a risk-based DevSecOps roadmap; establish ownership, metrics, escalation paths, and a plan to grow the team.
  • Implement preventive AWS controls for identity, networking, encryption, secrets/key management, and cloud configuration; ensure security-relevant activity is logged for monitoring, investigation, and audit.
  • Embed security into IaC, CI/CD, containers/orchestration, and software supply chains (SCA, secrets scanning, artifact integrity/signing, SBOMs where appropriate), including automated pipeline controls (SAST, IaC/container scanning, policy-as-code).
  • Partner with AppSec and InfoSec on security testing, policy, risk, audit evidence, and incident response.
  • Triage and prioritize vulnerabilities by exposure, exploitability, and business impact; coordinate remediation, track exceptions, and support investigation, containment, recovery, and post-incident improvement.

What We're Looking For

Required qualifications

  • 10+ years combined experience in software, platform/DevOps, and security engineering; 3+ years as a technical lead.
  • Experience leading cross-functional security or infrastructure initiatives and influencing engineering, DevOps/platform, AppSec, and InfoSec teams.
  • Hands-on AWS security and IAM (least privilege, service identities, privileged access, encryption, networking/security boundaries); experience automating controls with scripting, IaC, CI/CD, and policy-as-code.
  • Experience securing delivery pipelines end to end (IaC, CI/CD, containers, dependencies/artifacts, secrets).
  • Experience prioritizing vulnerabilities by risk and establishing ownership, escalation, exception, and remediation workflows.
  • Experience in security incident investigation, containment, recovery, and post-incident improvement; ability to communicate risk and tradeoffs to leadership.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience building a security/DevSecOps practice and hiring, developing, or managing engineers.
  • Kubernetes/container security; software supply chain and secure SDLC practices; security observability/detection partnership with InfoSec/SOC.
  • Experience selecting security tools, managing vendors and budgets, and measuring control coverage, risk reduction, and remediation progress.
  • Familiarity with public-company or regulated audit controls (e.g., SOX, SOC 2, ISO 27001).

BENEFITS & PERKS

  • Unlimited PTO
  • Excellent medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Employee Equity
  • Employee Discounts, Virtual Wellness Classes, and Pet Insurance and more!!

SALARY RANGE

The salary range for this role is $220,000 - $240,000, depending on location and experience.
